collection_summary: Multi-hop instance built from the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint: landlocked African countries → their bordering countries → those neighbors' official languages. The universe of 16 landlocked African countries comes from Wikidata directly via the all-ranks P31 path (`p:P31/ps:P31 wd:Q123480`) plus the continent filter (P30=Q15). Borders are P47 (shares border with), filtered to P31=Q6256 (country) to exclude non-state entities. Official languages are P37 (official language). Result: 224 rows × 3 columns, with composite PK on all three columns so each (country, neighbor, language) triple is a distinct evaluable row. (Cycle-3 repair: one non-language artifact — Wikidata's 'languages of Guinea' meta-item Q1339026 in Guinea's P37 — was filtered out, dropping the count from 225 to 224; see decision_log.)
source_coverage_notes: Single-source instance grounded entirely in Wikidata. The full universe of 16 landlocked African countries is recovered directly from Wikidata typing — no rows are supplemented. Row distribution is uneven by neighbor: South Africa (12 official languages including South African Sign Language) and Zimbabwe (Wikidata lists 16 official languages) account for the majority of rows for any landlocked country that borders them. Some neighbors are partially-recognized states (e.g., Somaliland, classified as Q6256 by Wikidata) — kept per Wikidata typing rather than excluded by political-recognition judgment. The 224-row total is the full closed-world Wikidata projection of this query after filtering one non-language artifact (Q1339026 'languages of Guinea' in Guinea's P37); see decision_log/verification_log.
decision_log: Chose multi_hop as the primary category because the data flow is a 3-link chain (landlocked → bordering → official-language) typical of recursive/chained-join semantics — exactly the stress that the multi_hop category targets. No secondary category assigned: the row shape is row-per-triple, not row-per-entity-with-multiple-attributes, so multi_attribute_projection does not fit. Composite PK on all three columns rather than (landlocked, neighbor) so each language is a distinct evaluable row, which produces more rows for confidence calibration. Chose Wikidata SPARQL (Tier A) over manual Wikipedia extraction because borders + official languages are well-typed Wikidata properties; the curation_protocol §4 explicitly recommends Tier A for multi_hop. The all-ranks P31 path was chosen for the landlocked-country universe clause specifically because some items (notably Rwanda, Q1037) record their `instance of: landlocked country` claim at normal rank rather than preferred rank, so the truthy `wdt:P31` path silently dropped them; the all-ranks path captures the same Wikidata claim regardless of rank ordering and yields the canonical 16-country set without any external supplementation. operation_type is 'join' to match the protocol/UI vocabulary for chained-join queries. SECONDARY_CATEGORY DECISION (re: cycle-1 audit SUGGESTION to omit/null the empty string): secondary_category is intentionally left as the empty string "". The curation UI validator (curation_ui/app.py validate_state) only errors when secondary_category is truthy AND equals query_category; an empty string is treated as 'no secondary category' and produces 0 errors / 0 warnings. The draft contract lists secondary_category as optional. No second category is an equally valid label for this row-per-triple multi_hop table, so leaving it empty is the honest state. Decision: keep empty; do not re-litigate. CYCLE-3 REPAIR (codex BLOCKING, 2026-06-03): Guinea's Wikidata P37 (official language) returns BOTH French (Q150) and the Wikimedia meta-item Q1339026 'languages of Guinea', which is not an actual language. The truthy wdt:P37 hop faithfully but wrongly included Q1339026, producing one spurious row 'Mali,Guinea,languages of Guinea'. Fix: added FILTER(?language != wd:Q1339026) to the staged .sparql and removed the single artifact row from the snapshot CSV (225 -> 224 rows); the correct value 'Mali,Guinea,French' is retained. No live regeneration (documented 2026-04-27 snapshot; regenerating would risk unrelated Wikidata drift). The auditor's F2-F4 were accepted as documented design decisions and are unchanged.
normalization_decisions: Country and language names follow Wikidata English labels (rdfs:label via the wikibase:label service). 'South African Sign Language' is kept verbatim as it is the Wikidata canonical label and one of South Africa's 12 official languages (statutorily added in 2023). 'Democratic Republic of the Congo' is kept full-form (not abbreviated 'DRC') per the curation_protocol §6 country normalization rule. The label service produced no unresolved QID fallback rows. The composite PK uses exact-string-match across all three columns; the evaluator must compare full canonical names.
verification_log: Cycle-2 curator re-verification against the live Wikidata Query Service (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql), accessed 2026-06-02, confirming the cycle-1 audit's two BLOCKING findings are resolved in the canonical artifacts: (A) operation_type is 'join', which is in OPERATION_TYPES and is one of the allowed ops for query_category=multi_hop ({join, filter}); the real curation_ui validate_state() returns 0 errors / 0 warnings. (B) BLOCKER-2 data verified at the source level, not just trusted: re-ran the staged SPARQL (all-ranks `p:P31/ps:P31 wd:Q123480` universe path, no Rwanda UNION) live and diffed against the staged CSV — 225 vs 225 rows, set-equal, 0 triples only in staged, 0 only in live, staged CSV already in canonical ORDER BY (landlocked, neighbor, language) order. Rwanda root-cause confirmed directly from Q1037 P31 statements: Q123480 'landlocked country' is recorded at NormalRank while country/republic/sovereign-state are PreferredRank, so truthy wdt:P31 omits it. Universe-size control: truthy wdt:P31 + P30=Q15 returns 15 landlocked African countries (Rwanda absent); all-ranks p:P31/ps:P31 + P30=Q15 returns 16 (Rwanda present); the difference is exactly {Rwanda}. The canonical 16-country set matches the standard list (Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Central African Republic, Chad, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Lesotho, Malawi, Mali, Niger, Rwanda, South Sudan, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). Internal-consistency sweep across all 225 rows: 0 self-borders (landlocked != bordering everywhere), 0 duplicate composite PKs, 0 blank cells, 0 QID-shaped label values; Lesotho's only neighbor is South Africa (enclave, correct), South Africa carries 12 official languages and Zimbabwe 16 (matches audit). No CSV, draft.json, or SPARQL value was changed in this cycle — the prior repair was found correct on independent re-verification. Independence note: this is a curator self-verification, NOT a Ready certification; an independent Codex auditor must run cycle-2 audit before the instance is locked. CYCLE-3 NOTE (2026-06-03): the cycle-2 live diff reported 225=225 set-equal because BOTH the staged CSV and the live query contained the Q1339026 'languages of Guinea' artifact (Guinea's P37 includes the meta-item), so the diff could not flag it. The independent codex audit identified Q1339026 as a non-language artifact. After adding FILTER(?language != wd:Q1339026) and removing the one artifact row, the row count is 224; PK-uniqueness, no-self-border, no-blank-cell, and no-QID-label invariants re-checked clean on the 224-row set.
open_questions: 0) STATUS: Both cycle-1 audit BLOCKING findings (operation_type=multi_join outside vocabulary; Rwanda partially_supplemented rationale inaccurate) are resolved in the canonical artifacts AND independently re-verified against live Wikidata in cycle-2 (see verification_log). An independent codex audit subsequently found one BLOCKING factual artifact (the Wikidata meta-item Q1339026 'languages of Guinea' in Guinea's P37); resolved in cycle-3 (added FILTER(?language != wd:Q1339026); removed the one artifact row; 225 -> 224). Awaiting independent re-audit for the 0/0/0 lock. 1) South Africa's 12 official languages and Zimbabwe's 16 inflate row counts for any landlocked country that borders them, which means the per-country evaluation signal will be dominated by these two neighbors. Down-weighting strategies (e.g., evaluate per (landlocked, neighbor) pair rather than per triple) are a downstream metric question, not a curation issue. 2) Some neighbors are partially-recognized states (e.g., Somaliland classified as Q6256). Kept by Wikidata typing rather than judged separately. If a future repair wants to exclude partially-recognized states, document that policy here and re-run with a stricter filter (e.g., exclude entities with Q15634554 'state with limited recognition'). 3) Wikidata's P37 may include languages with limited regional or de jure status (e.g., national vs. official distinction). For this instance, P37 was taken at face value as 'official language' per Wikidata convention. 4) The all-ranks P31 path is sensitive to Wikidata rank-curation choices: if a future Wikidata edit demotes a Q123480 statement to deprecated rank, this query will still include it. Periodic re-runs should compare the count against the expected 16.
